evidence.quote:
def item_count(self) -> int:
        return sum(item.quantity for item in self.items)

criteria.reasoning: sum() over an empty generator returns the int 0. The dedicated test builds a fresh Cart, checks item_count() == 0 and passed in the gate.

evidence.quote: return sum(item.quantity for item in self.items)

cart.add(LineItem("apple", Decimal("0.50"), 2))
    cart.add(LineItem("pear", Decimal("1.25"), 3))

    assert cart.item_count() == 5

criteria.reasoning: The method adds up the quantities rather than counting lines, which matches the answer to Q-001. The test adds two lines with quantities 2 and 3, checks the count is 5 and passed. A line-counting version would return 2 and fail this test, so the test tells the two readings apart.

test_adequacy.reason: It calls item_count() on a freshly created Cart and checks that the result is 0.
It adds lines with quantities 2 and 3 and checks the count is 5, which tells summing quantities apart from counting lines.
The test adds items before it checks anything, so it never looks at the count of a new cart. Its trace to the New cart criterion is wrong.

findings.title: Quantity-sum test is wrongly traced to the New cart criterion
findings.detail: test_item_count_sums_line_item_quantities is marked @pytest.mark.l4("C-cab85837", "C-bc4c166e"), but it never checks a new cart's count of 0. The traceability matrix therefore overstates coverage of C-bc4c166e. The criterion is still covered by test_new_cart_item_count_is_zero.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop C-bc4c166e from the marker on test_item_count_sums_line_item_quantities.

findings.title: No scenario says whether a discount code affects the item count
findings.detail: item_count() reads only the quantities in self.items, so an applied discount code has no effect on it. No scenario pins this down. An implementation that ties the count to the priced total would behave differently.

evidence.quote: return sum(item.quantity for item in self.items)

findings.suggested_fix: WHEN a discount code has been applied to a cart holding line items with quantities 2 and 3 THEN its item count is still 5.

riskiest_assumptions: That Cart.add appends the LineItem to self.items unchanged, so item_count sees each added quantity (the diff does not show add, but the passing test is consistent with this).
That the gate report reflects the committed head, and that the passing tests ran the item_count shown in the diff.
That LineItem.quantity is a plain int, so the sum is an int and 0 compares equal to the expected count.
